verdict.line: You win if you force all-ins before Nasus stacks his Q and gets Fury of the Sands online; you lose if you let him free-farm into a late-game duelist.

brief.thesis: Nasus has zero dash, blink, or disengage in his whole kit, which is exactly what Sett's stun-and-burst toolkit is built to punish — but Nasus's Siphoning Strike (Q) is a linear scaling clock that eventually closes the gap, and that tension is why 1,820 games of this matchup sit almost dead even at 49.8% despite Sett holding the nominal lane and solo-kill edge. Whoever controls the first 10 levels of the wave decides which version of this lane you get.

theirWindow.what: Don't commit to a long auto-trade once Wither lands — it decelerates your Move and Attack Speed over time, so close distance fast using Q's bonus move speed and finish your combo before the slow stacks up, or back off entirely.

yourWindow.when: Nasus's W and E are both down
yourWindow.what: All-in with Q's bonus-damage autos into E (Facebreaker), positioned so a minion sits on Nasus's far side for the real stun instead of just a slow, then release W's stored Grit for the shield-punch finish — Nasus has no dash and cannot escape.

start.why: Highest-picked start at 86.9% with a 50.3% win rate over 2,101 games — the sustain and attack damage keep you even in prolonged early trades against Nasus's lifesteal.

boots.why: 53.8% win rate over 718 games, well above Plated Steelcaps here — the flat tenacity-style slow resistance directly blunts Wither so you can still close distance and finish combos.

core.why: The proc's attack-move slow sticks on an immobile target, letting you force the all-in before he can walk away.
On-hit armor shred compounds with Nasus's own health-stacking, keeping your damage relevant as he builds tankier.
Highest-winrate finisher at 59.3% in this combo over 423 games — the bonus health and burn damage scale to match Nasus's late health pool.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks through Sett's back-and-forth trading and Q's bonus-damage autos, and the healing at max stacks outlasts Nasus's Soul Eater lifesteal in extended lane skirmishes.

summoners.why: Most-picked combo at 90% with a 50.2% win rate — Ignite closes the kill window on a target with free lifesteal before Soul Eater heals it back, and Flash sets up or escapes Wither's slow.

playing.title: Punish before level 6
playing.detail: Force trades levels 1-5 using Q's bonus-damage autos and W's stored Grit shield. Nasus has no dash, so he can't disengage from a committed skirmish.

playing.title: Starve his Q stacks
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike only grows stronger off kills, so freezing the wave or contesting last hits directly denies his scaling clock — this is OP.GG's own call on the matchup.

playing.title: Use E with a minion present
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are on opposite sides of you; alone, Nasus is just slowed. Fight with a minion wave between you so the stun actually lands.

playing.title: Don't trade into Wither
playing.detail: Wither decelerates your Move and Attack Speed over time at 700 range. If it's up, close the gap fast with Q's move speed and finish quickly or disengage.

playing.title: Fight off his Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Standing in the Spirit Fire zone strips your armor too, amplifying his physical damage — fight at the edge or bait him into using it early.

playing.title: Pick your Show Stopper spot
playing.detail: The Show Stopper slams Nasus down and slows everyone near the landing point, so land it away from jungle camps or allies that could save him, not just the instant it's off cooldown.

playing.title: Respect him after level 6
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands grants bonus health, range, and drains nearby max health into damage — don't extend fights near minions once he's hit 6.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, runes, and win-rate figures above come from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical breakdown and timing calls are my own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow during early game by applying pressure and gaining lane control. Use your abilities whenever the come off cooldown to deal damage.
